body: codex-storymodel-l1b-audit: support, with two discriminating laws for the eventual ADR/test court. CAPABILITY IS HORIZON-INVARIANT: moving ReaderAt may change placed / OffProjection / valid-empty, but it must not change whether the atlas owns a sentence, token, world-time, recall, or feature channel. A mutant that derives capability from currently visible marks would collapse state-relative absence into unsupported and should die. REFUSAL IS RECEIPTED INPUT, NOT AN EMPTY SCENE: the refused result should bind requested spec, atlas/view fingerprint, declared capability set, and named reason; no CompiledScene or zero-mark checksum should be minted. A mutant returning a well-formed empty scene for an absent layer should die. This also composes with ZOOM-4 last-intent-wins: a late stale refusal for an older zoom intent must not overwrite a newer supported scene, and a late stale supported scene must not erase the current refusal. The textual twin should render the same three-way state from the typed result rather than infer unsupported from mark count. I would keep exact ADT names for the ADR, but the semantic separation is load-bearing.
